summary: Deterministically refine derived volume samples with compliant length, bending, root and contact constraints.
x-minimum-refinement: Run at least two refinement steps before residual-based early completion so neighbouring parameter values do not select a visibly different one-step result. The configured budget remains a hard maximum.
x-contact-bounds: A query outside a distance grid's padded bounds has at least the 30 mm padding as positive clearance, even when an open source boundary's oriented sign is negative. It cannot be projected onto the grid box.
x-contact-surface: The worker welds coincident collision vertices and caps unambiguous open boundary loops before building signed distance. Determine inside by oriented scanline crossings of the closed collision surface; a nearest triangle's normal cannot supply a reliable sign at a neck edge. Rendered and scalp-binding topology remain unchanged. Open neck and crop boundaries must not produce false inside regions or unstable outward directions.
x-segment-gradient: Distribute a segment contact correction to both endpoints using closest-point barycentric weights and inverse masses. Root and convergence holds have zero inverse mass. Sending all correction to the tip can stretch short foreground fibres and is invalid.
x-contact-prototype: Compare triangle-distance fields with a closed occupancy field followed by an anisotropic Euclidean distance transform. Closing narrow voxel gaps is a collision approximation and its spatial error must be reported; neither approach changes rendered geometry. Keep the method that satisfies contact and continuity on all regression grooms.
x-contact-union: Head and torso grids sample the same union solid at different resolutions and overlapping spatial query domains. Internal neck caps are not collision surfaces. A fine grid owns the head and neck; the torso field owns the remaining region, with overlap. Residuals report every active query domain, including a zero-sample domain explicitly.
x-continuation: Sequential scalar edits warm-start from the previous matching solved paths with the same fibre attachments. Reset, geometry and graph-topology changes start cold. The previous state is explicit process input; test warm edit sequences separately from cold determinism.
x-cut-continuation: A cold solve is styled and settled before trimming. Its terminated fibre lengths and cut-tip plane become explicit continuation state. Warm edits retain that termination and constrain the tip to the plane, avoiding a jump to a different curve/plane crossing. Shortening below the terminated length releases that tip constraint. The authored intrinsic length map remains unchanged.
x-tip-curl: When a cut plane exists, apply tip curl locally after the initial settled trim, then relax contact and length with the cut-tip plane retained. Curling an entire uncut fibre toward the neck before trimming can trap it above the cut and create discontinuous terminations. Without a cut, the existing intrinsic tip-region field applies.
x-cut-budget: Prepare the curled cut against contact, reducing its local deformation where blocked. Measure the resulting retained intrinsic distances before discarding the unused tail; retained length cannot exceed the original fibre budget. Merge terminal spans shorter than twice contact clearance while preserving their intrinsic sum. A cut tip has zero inverse mass along the plane normal in length constraints and length sweeps.
x-refinement-demand: After the two fixed initial steps, refine only fibres whose contact or length residual still fails. Already accepted fibres receive no further gravity or work. This policy is per-fibre data, never a style branch.
x-execution: Pure bounded numerical batches run inside the generation worker process, with cancellation observed between batches.
x-contact: Cache a head/ear signed-distance grid per geometry revision in the worker; fitted shoulder/neck capsules; query segment interiors as well as endpoints and report final residuals.
x-constraints: Fixed step and order, step-scaled compliance, accumulated multipliers, pinned roots, rest-shape bending and limited sample-bundle separation; no authored guides and no runtime Dyng claims.
x-frame: Static solve in bind-pose head space with bind-pose down vector; generated output follows Head rigidly, dynamic motion is M4.
